title: Crash during profiling

labels.name: bug-crash
labels.description: issue reporting a crash or segfault

body:
<!-- Before reporting: search existing issues and check the FAQ. -->

- `nvim --version`: NVIM v0.5.0-d2766b0
- `vim -u DEFAULTS` (version: ) behaves differently? Does not crash.
- Operating system/version: Arch Linux

### Steps to reproduce using `nvim -u NORC`

**UPDATE 2:** In one file: [The malicious script.](https://gist.github.com/zsugabubus/60f354fa9a3ee5ae8f9435fa8388ebb8) [Repo.](https://github.com/zsugabubus/nvim-crash)

---

* `nvim -u NORC`
* Open your ‘init.vim’ (or some Vim file).
* [`packadd vim-white`](https://github.com/zsugabubus/vim-white) (will start profiling into ‘white.log’).
* [`packadd vim-commentr`](https://github.com/zsugabubus/vim-commentr).
* Press <kbd>K</kbd> on some function (maybe relevant).
* Hit <kbd>Enter</kbd> until all red goes away (`vim-white` generates a bunch of error messages, so will not call `profile stop`).
* Go back to your opened Vim file.
* <kbd>Leader</kbd><kbd>c</kbd><kbd>c</kbd>.
* Crash.

Sorry, for the little self-promotion but really this is the way it crashes. `packadd` was easy to me, but probably works as “expected” using `source` too.

**UPDATE:** commentr no longer needed. You can enjoy the never ending fun using `--cmd 'source happy.vim'`. (white still required to generate errors.)
```vim
" happy.vim
nnoremap X :call X()<CR>
fun X()
	new
	set ft=vim
endfun
```

So the one-liner:
```sh
nvim -u NORC +'h nextnonblank' --cmd 'packadd vim-white' --cmd 'source happy.vim' '+normal X'
```
